newsitem.title: USA: Petroecuador declares force majeure on Oriente.
newsitem.headline: Petroecuador declares force majeure on Oriente.

text.p: Ecuador's state oil company Petroecuador has declared force majeure on Oriente crude cargoes loading in March, a company official said on Thursday.
The official said eight to 10 cargoes would be affected.
Petroecuador declared force majeure after a pump on the main Transecuadoran pipeline exploded on March 7, curtailing pumping operations until March 12.
Pumping is now back to normal, the official said.
The affected cargoes amount to about half of the normal loading program.
"We communicated to our customers that the whole March program was affected, but now that pumping is back to normal, not all the cargoes will be affected," the official said.
Petroecuador normally exports about 20 cargoes of Oriente per month.
Petroecuador notified customers that the affected cargoes would be delivered with a minimum of 360,000 barrels per cargo guaranteed, the official said.
He added that the force majeure declaration would probably be lifted in the next day or two once the company is sure pumping operations are stabilized.
Among the affected companies was Chile's state-owned Empresa Nacional del Petroleo (ENAP), which had three cargoes contracted for loading in March.
Two of the cargoes were contracted through Argentine trading house Interpetrol and one from Swiss-based trader Glencore.
Ecuador produces about 380,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude and exports some 240,000 bpd.
